summary.headline: NCC Q4 FY26 standalone turnover fell 1% to INR5,382 crores; consolidated order book hit a record INR83,004 crores, but no FY27 guidance was given.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 turnover rose 1% YoY to INR6,251 crores, while full-year consolidated turnover fell 6% to INR20,944 crores and standalone fell 9% to INR17,669 crores. Consolidated order book reached INR83,004 crores (about 16% up YoY), with Q4 inflows of INR9,573 crores. Margins compressed YoY: consolidated EBITDA 8.83% vs 9.07%, and PAT 3.3% vs 4.1%. Management declined to give FY27 guidance on revenue, margin, order inflow, capex or working capital, citing an uncertain environment, and said it would revisit after Q1. Debt-to-equity improved to 0.30x from 0.40x in Q3, and JJM (UP) receivables fell sharply after roughly INR1,000 crores of collections.

segments.name: Buildings
segments.commentary: Standalone order book INR22,740 crores as at March 2026, the largest vertical by book value.

segments.name: Transportation
segments.commentary: Standalone order book INR15,320 crores; includes GMLR Mumbai project of about INR3,000 crores, for which TBM is being deployed.

segments.name: Water and Railways
segments.commentary: Standalone order book INR10,400 crores; UP Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) order book INR6,181 crores pending across groundwater and surface water, with INR20,142 crores executed of INR26,000 crores total JJM orders received.

segments.name: Mining
segments.commentary: Consolidated mining order book about INR15,000 crores (standalone INR6,750 crores after Pachhwara Coal Mining adjustment). Pachhwara MDO mine running at 15 MTPA rated capacity, revenue above INR2,000 crores; new mining award above INR6,000 crores to flow through standalone from FY27.

segments.name: Smart meters (T&D)
segments.commentary: Standalone order book INR4,456 crores; consolidated INR646 crores. INR460 crores invested in two SPVs, fully funded per management.

guidance_outlook: No guidance for FY27 on revenue, margin, order inflow, capex, working capital or net debt; management will revisit after Q1 FY27 (around 3-4 months).
FY27 standalone capex planned at INR500 crores: about INR350-400 crores maintenance and replenishment, and INR100-150 crores for mining equipment.
TBM for GMLR expected to be capitalised at end of Q2 FY27; depreciation to rise from Q3 FY27, with TBM capex (about INR320 crores) to be depreciated over roughly 3 years.
Management said about 74% of contracts have escalation clauses but may not fully cover cost increases; some margin impact is expected.
Vizag Urban receivable of about INR250 crores expected in FY27 (outstanding INR291 crores).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR912 crores against revised budget of INR1,050 crores (previously INR750 crores), including about INR320 crores for TBM; Q4 capex INR344 crores.
Pachhwara mine (15 MTPA rated capacity achieved in FY23-24) is expected to hold similar output and revenue/profit range in FY27.
Pipeline of bid-able infrastructure projects estimated by management at about INR2.5 lakh crores.
About INR1,700 crores of new orders reported in April 2026 (FY27 to date).
demand_pricing: Consolidated order book INR83,004 crores at 31 March 2026 (highest in company history), book-to-bill about 4x; FY26 inflows INR31,884 crores.
Q4 consolidated inflows INR9,573 crores vs standalone inflows INR4,775 crores; difference of about INR4,800 crores is Pachhwara Coal Mining, booked on a 3-year look-ahead basis.
Government clients (central, state, PSUs, agencies) about 95% of order book; private about 5%. No private client pressure or cancellations reported.
Management said there is no payment issue from private or other clients; Q4 saw improvement in payment cycles.
Management said order book execution is not constrained by resources or clearances; the 45-day run-rate of execution is normal per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give FY27 guidance on revenue, margin and order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: No guidance for FY27 on any parameter given the uncertain environment; management will revisit after Q1 FY27 once there is more clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Is execution slowing and are clients asking to slow down work?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said all orders in the INR80,000-83,000 crore book have clearances and are fully available for execution, with no holdups.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables and payment status for JJM (UP) projects?
qa_highlights.answer: UP JJM receivables fell to INR3,015 crores (incl. unbilled), with trade receivables at INR695 crores vs about INR1,700 crores in December; about INR1,000 crores collected in Q4 and INR400-450 crores in April.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone order book split and smart meter book?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone order book INR72,259 crores; subsidiary INR10,745 crores. Smart meter book INR4,456 crores standalone and INR646 crores consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the FY26 finance cost jump and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 finance cost INR645 crores (3.7% of revenue): loan interest INR220 crores, mobilisation advance interest INR154 crores, BG/LC commissions INR162 crores, other bank charges INR109 crores. Net of interest income INR554 crores (3.18%). Management would not estimate forward finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to subsidiaries and smart-meter funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in subsidiaries INR887 crores and loans to group companies INR309 crores at March 2026. Smart-meter SPVs have INR460 crores invested; SBI loan of about INR1,100 crores at 9.15%.

risks_watch: Input cost, logistics and fuel price inflation; escalation clauses cover about 74% of contracts, so margin compression beyond recovery is possible.
Material availability risk; company is buying materials just-in-time.
Payment cycle for UP JJM receivables and any impact of current developments on client payments; finance cost could rise if payments slow.
Execution pace over the next quarter; management said no FY27 view until Q1 results.
Pending arbitrations and sub judice Jubilee Hills project; Oman impairment INR21.3 crores booked as exceptional item and all international receivables now fully impaired.
summary.management_tone: Cautious and somewhat evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to guide, citing an uncertain macro environment and promising a revisit after Q1. It was more confident on historic execution, order book quality, collections and government exposure.
key_quotes: So we have decided not to give any guidance for FY27.
There is absolutely no issue on account of any holdups or resigns or write-off bases.
In Q4, we have seen improvement in the payment cycle. Absolutely, that is correct.
